messages:
incident-bot: PAGED @sara_oncall - Dedicated cluster ded-hz-03 reporting sustained elevated 5xx and gateway_timeouts for tenant horizonburst. Severity: P1. Please acknowledge and triage. :rotating_light:

sara_oncall: acked. I'm on it, pulling metrics and logs now. Anyone already on rotation for ded-hz-03?

alex_sre: I can join. Seeing increase in 5xx rate from 00:10 UTC onwards. Dashboard (link): https://redwood.internal/ded-hz-03/metrics - request latency and 5xx spike correlate with inflight queue depth.

sara_oncall: thanks. Maria, can you confirm if customer-facing alerts were fired?

maria_support: customer alerts sent at 00:14 UTC. Kevin from HorizonBurst replied "we're seeing timeouts on inference calls, heavy retry storms". He's on thread (cc @kevin_customer).

kevin_customer: yep. Our app saw a surge of 504s and 502s across a handful of endpoints, started ~2 minutes after your bot page. Key thing: model variant hudson-v2 was being used heavily during a batch job. Not intentional but bursty.

jin_prodeng: that sounds like classic noisy neighbor. Checking GPU utilization and KV cache evictions on node pool. Running quick query: `kubectl top pods -n ded-hz-03 | sort -rnk 3 | head` shows two pods at 96% GPU and increasing NVMe IO. Also high KV miss/eviction rate.

alex_sre: can we throttle or isolate tenant traffic? We have per-tenant routing policies for Dedicated. Suggest two-pronged approach: 1) route HorizonBurst to burst-throttle tier (reduce concurrency), 2) provision short-lived burst capacity if autoscale can spin up within SLA.

sara_oncall: initiate canary routing change now? If we push route to degraded model variant (hudson-v1-quantized) customers might see quality reg change. Kevin, any objections to fallback to v1 quantized for 5m while we stabilize?

kevin_customer: quality drop is acceptable short-term if it restores availability. Please keep us updated.

ops-bot: executed route-change: horizonburst -> hudson-v1-quantized (5m) by sara_oncall. Rollback in 5m or manual.

maria_support: support note: informed customer success + postmortem on standby.

jin_prodeng: I pushed an eviction filter to the scheduler to deprioritize background batch jobs for that tenant pool. Command run: ```
# temporary patch
kubectl patch scheduler ded-hz-03 -p '{"spec":{"evictionFilter":{"labelsNotIn":["batch-job"]}}}'
```

alex_sre: after throttle + eviction filter, 5xx rate dropped ~70% in 90s. Latency tail reduced. Still seeing a few gateway timeouts as in-flight KV cache thrash recovers.

sara_oncall: good. Start gradual reconnect to primary variant after 3m if stable. Jin, any telemetry on KV hit rate?

jin_prodeng: KV hit rate improving from 41% -> 78% over last 2m. NVMe write queue depth falling. GPU saturated pod count down to 1. Looks healthy.

sara_oncall: ok let's extend degraded route for another 3m to be safe, then test 10% traffic to original variant. Monitor errors and be ready to revert.

ops-bot: route-change: horizonburst -> hudson-v1-quantized extended by sara_oncall for +3m.

alex_sre: starting 10% canary to hudson-v2 primary now. Observability: spike in 5xx when canary began; rolled back to 0% after 25s. Back to 100% degraded.

sara_oncall: rollback expected. Any longterm mitigation? We should schedule tenant-level rate limits for background batch jobs and a quota for model-concurrency for Dedicated customers. File infra task?

jin_prodeng: filing infra task: "dedicated: tenant-concurrency-quotas + scheduler eviction rules" and will attach telemetry.

maria_support: customer update posted: "We detected elevated errors caused by a high-volume background job on your account. We applied a temporary fallback to a lower-cost model variant and evicted batch jobs to restore availability. We're working on permanent quotas to prevent recurrence."

kevin_customer: thanks, appreciate quick action. Please share ETA for permanent fix.

sara_oncall: ETA for quotas & scheduler changes: initial design 3d, rollout to staging 5d, prod 10d. I'll add Kevin to the RFC when ready.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: resolved for now. Root cause: tenant-driven batch workload causing noisy neighbor effects (GPU saturation, KV cache thrash). Mitigation: routing fallback, scheduler eviction filter, temporary throttle. Postmortem assigned.

maria_support: capturing CS impact: estimated customer error-window ~4 minutes, ~1.2K failed requests, no data exfiltration.

alex_sre: next actions: 1) prod postmortem, 2) implement tenant concurrency quotas, 3) add runbook step to apply eviction filter + fallback routing, 4) make short-lived burst autoscale faster. I'll own runbook updates.

sara_oncall: thanks everyone. I'll hand off to oncall-next and close page. @ops-bot please mark incident handoff to next-oncall.

ops-bot: handoff complete. Incident thread closed by sara_oncall.
